interest: This document provides insight into U.S. diplomatic monitoring of bilateral agreements and Japanese immigration policy in Latin America during the interwar period. It reflects Cuban sensitivity or U.S. interest regarding the legal status and entry privileges of Japanese subjects in Cuba, showing official Cuban assurances that treaty provisions did not expand immigration rights beyond existing domestic law. It also demonstrates State Department cross-referencing practices between Japanese internal affairs (894) and Latin American bilateral treaty files (637.9431).
overview: This file comprises a single State Department Document File Note (cross-reference sheet) dated May 2, 1930, filed under classification 894.5537 (Immigration to Japan from Cuba). The sheet cross-references Despatch No. 192 from American diplomatic officer Reed in Cuba (filed under decimal number 637.9431/4), which reports on immigration privileges stipulated in an agreement between Cuba and Japan. The note records an assurance from Cuban official Mr. Ortiz that the agreement does not confer upon Japanese subjects any rights or privileges beyond those already granted under existing Cuban legislation.
